reader_contract.primary_reader: A Californian considering a skilled-trade career: a recent graduate, a career changer, or an apprentice choosing a specialization.
reader_contract.sophistication_level: Early-career or career-changing, comfortable with salary data but unfamiliar with California licensing and apprenticeship routes.
reader_contract.trigger_problem: Salary lists online mix job-board estimates, national averages and non-trade roles, so the reader cannot tell which California trades actually pay the most or how to get into them.
reader_contract.existing_belief: Trades pay well but the reader does not know which ones clear six figures in California or how long the training takes.
reader_contract.decision_task_helped: Shortlist two or three California trades by pay, training time, licensing path and demand.
reader_contract.distinctive_angle: A California-only ranking from one official 2025 dataset with median and top-10-percent pay, paired with the official training and licensing route for every trade.
reader_contract.promised_payoff: A defensible, sourced shortlist of high-paying California trades and the first step into each.
exclusions: job-board salary estimates or figures mixed from different datasets
engineering, management, coordinator and general contractor roles in the ranked list
links to the national highest-paying-trade-jobs blog or to competitor articles on the same topic
customer outcomes, reviews, testimonials or Hindsight deal data presented as proof
named author or Person schema without approved authorship evidence
first-person authority language, editorial-process commentary, or em dashes in public copy
